title: Huawei's patent application for ternary logic gate circuits
excerpt:
If the Soviet Union's ternary computers had not been stifled, what would today's AI revolution look like? When the pointer of history turns to 2025, Huawei's patent application for ternary logic gate circuits is rewriting the script of human computing civilization. Just like submitting the underlying architecture innovation for public release in March 2025 in September 2023, it may reshape the game rules of the entire semiconductor industry. The mathematical charm of the ternary system lies in its natural symmetry, which is different from the binary 0 and 13 systems that use a balanced system of -1, 0, and 1. This design makes the expression of numbers closer to the true, false, and unknown states of human thinking.

As early as 1958, Moscow University in the Soviet Union developed the world's first ternary computer, which consumed only one-third of the power of binary devices of the same period and had astonishing operational stability. However, under the suppression of the bureaucratic system, this disruptive product was forcibly shut down due to its threat to the existing interest chain, becoming the most regrettable regret in the history of Cold War technology. Huawei's breakthrough lies precisely in solving the technological gap that the Soviet Union failed to bridge. Through innovative logic gate circuit design, the number of transistors has been reduced by more than 30%, and energy consumption has been reduced to one-third of traditional binary. This innovation of reconstructing computing logic from the physical layer has opened up a new path for improving the energy efficiency of AI chips. More noteworthy is the natural compatibility between ternary and quantum computing, which may lay the groundwork for the next generation of information technology revolution.

Huawei is opening up an unprecedented track. Nvidia CEO Huang Renxun admitted in a recent interview that while Western tech giants are still relying on stacked transistors to boost computing power, Huawei's ternary patent has quietly touched upon the original problem of chip design - how to achieve higher efficiency with fewer resources. If this technology can be widely commercialized, it will not only restructure the energy consumption standards of electronic devices, but may also give rise to a new computing ecosystem. From 5G to Starflash, from quantum computing to ternary chips, Huawei is using a series of hardcore innovations to prove that the key to breaking through technological barriers lies in mastering the discourse power of the underlying architecture. When the spark of ternary is reigniting in the East, we may be witnessing the dawn of a new era of computing. What kind of changes will happen to our electronic devices if ternary chips are widely applied?

title: How to respond to societal collapse | Sarah Wilson | TEDxSydney
excerpt:
Science and modelling shows our civilisation is in existential collapse, but what if this terrifying reality is the prod that humanity needs to live fully and in attainment again? In this provocative talk, international best-selling author and journalist Sarah Wilson explores the upside of losing what we’ve been taking for granted.  Sarah Wilson is a multi-New York Times and Amazon best-selling author, podcaster, social philosopher and renegade. 

She is the host of the podcast Wild with Sarah Wilson and writes the popular Substack newsletter This is Precious, which has an engaged community of 57,000 subscribers. 

Sarah is known globally for founding the I Quit Sugar movement - a digital wellness program and 13 award-winning books that sell in 52 countries - which saw millions around the world transform their health. In 2022 Sarah sold the business and donated 100 per cent of the proceeds to charity.

Her New York Times bestseller First, We Make the Beast Beautiful is described by Mark Manson as “the best book on living with anxiety that I’ve ever read” and was featured as a book of the year on NBC’s Today Show. Her book This One Wild & Precious Life won the 2021 US Gold Nautilus Award. 

Sarah is an advisor to corporations and universities on media, mental health and existential risk. She’s guest lectured for the University of Cambridge’s Sustainability and Leadership masters course and partnered with organisations such as the Climate Council, Harvard University and Intelligence Squared on campaigns. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
